pattern: Only 1 of the 10 runs in this chunk is a real misranking. Opus OCFLB-CHART-01-ADAPTER run-002 put the H4 decoy rim first and the gold nudge second. It read every hop body through 'grep -A' starting at the signature, so it never saw the javadocs that state the drift convention, it never opened the pin, and it never ran the test. It then settled the sign inverse pair with the upstream (p1-p2)*pct prior: CONVENTION_PRIOR, with EVIDENCE_RETRIEVAL_FAILURE as the secondary mode. The other 9 are Sonnet runs that never committed to an answer, although every one of them displayed the gold fault line, at steps 9-21: 4 hit the 50-call limit, 4 hit the 300 s timeout, and 1 (COMPRESS-07-DEFINER run-005) submitted the gold at rank 1 but was rejected because its rank-9 filler, ExtraFieldUtils::merge, does not exist; it ran out of calls before resubmitting. None of the 9 shows a misattribution. In 3 of them (MATH-06-ADAPTER run-001, MATH-06-DEFINER run-002 and COMPRESS-07-DEFINER run-005) the agent's own tool output had already named the correct method. The budget went on four things: hunting for a test harness (mvn, ant, junit jars, up to 'find /'); verifying values far from the fault (JacksonCore parser offsets, the bicubic AINV algebra); re-reading hops it had already read; and probing git history (git log/show/diff on the outer repository in 3 JacksonCore runs, which is a protocol breach that reached the adversarial-break-v1 commit text). A stale defects4j.build.properties (classes.modified=NumberInput,TextBuffer) also sent one run off course. Pins were almost never consulted: only JACKSONCORE-10-DEFINER run-003 opened one, at its very last calls. Two isolation gaps showed up. First, /tmp is shared across runs: JACKSONCORE-10-DEFINER run-001 ran ProbeJackson488, which another run had left in /tmp, so the annotation's 'self-written probe' is wrong. Second, the workspaces sit inside the outer git repository, so git log works from inside them. Overall, for Sonnet the dominant failure in this chunk is over-verification under a fixed call and time budget, not attribution. The definer bias appears only in the Opus run, where the convention is settled by a prior instead of the javadoc.
